title: Anant National University Students to Design Pedestrian Bridge for NHAI in Ahmedabad
summary: Anant National University students will design a pedestrian bridge proposed by NHAI at Narol Crossroad, Ahmedabad, through a three-stage design competition.
body_html:
Ahmedabad, 29 October 2026: Students of Anant National University will develop the design for a pedestrian bridge proposed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) at Narol Crossroad in Ahmedabad. The collaboration takes design education beyond the classroom and into a live public infrastructure project.

The initiative is open to Anant students across disciplines and will invite proposals through a three-stage design competition. Participants will be asked to produce a practical and implementable bridge design, while exploring how thoughtful design can improve usability, visual appeal and the everyday experience of people using public infrastructure. The final selected proposal will be awarded and taken forward in close collaboration with NHAI.

The project is being led at the university by Dr Sanjeev Vidyarthi, Provost, and Ar Jabeen Zacharias, Professor of Practice. Shri Pradeep Atri, CGM (Tech) and Regional Officer, NHAI, and architect Habeeb Khan are also closely involved.

Speaking about the initiative, Dr Sanjeev Vidyarthi said, “Anant National University is committed to providing purposeful design education where students have the opportunity to work with the complexities of the real world. Designing for a real public site, the proposed pedestrian bridge in this case, is an example of that pedagogical approach. Such public spaces are part of the everyday experience for millions of city dwellers, and their design must respond to questions of people, place, safety, usability and the larger urban context. Collaborations like these offer our students the unique opportunity to learn to negotiate real constraints, engage with multiple stakeholders and understand what it takes to move an idea from the drawing board towards implementation.”

Unlike academic briefs that stay within the classroom, the project will expose students to the processes involved in preparing a design for implementation. As their proposals move through the competition stages, they will deal with practical requirements, design iterations and the considerations involved in turning an idea into a workable public structure.

Ar Jabeen Zacharias added, “Design is zero until it works for people. The ‘Imagine’ initiative, conceived to harvest ideas for people-oriented design, encourages students to understand and respond to people and contexts, with design as an instrument for positive change in society. A pedestrian bridge is a simple example, an everyday structure where a thoughtful intervention can transform how people experience and engage with it for the better. This collaboration with the National Highways Authority of India marks an important moment for Anant, a stepping stone into the national design scene, bringing interdisciplinary design thinking into public infrastructure. It is a significant moment where collaboration, design and education come together to touch everyday lives.”

By opening the challenge to students from different disciplines, the university hopes to encourage varied approaches to the brief. Selected students will also gain first-hand exposure to how public projects evolve through collaboration among designers, technical experts, institutions and implementing agencies.
